description: Signed PortLock security events: the interoperability contract between PortLock (Python, portlock/audit/signing.py) and ClawNet (JavaScript). Every implementation must accept each entry of 'valid' and reject each entry of 'invalid'. Generated by PortLock's own code from the fixed test seeds below and re-verified by tests/unit/test_audit_signing.py.
encoding_of_this_file: Pure ASCII JSON. Non-ASCII characters in strings are written as \uXXXX escapes (surrogate pairs above U+FFFF), so a JSON parser yields the intended text whatever the editor or checkout did. The signed bytes are NOT escaped like this: they are the UTF-8 in 'canonical_b64'.

signing.algorithm: ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure Ed25519, no context, no prehash)
signing.signed_bytes: prefix_hex as bytes, followed by the canonical JSON (UTF-8) of the event with its 'sig' member removed
signing.canonical_json: RFC 8785 restricted to ASCII object keys and integers in the IEEE-754 safe range: keys sorted by code unit, no whitespace, minimal string escaping, no Unicode normalisation. Vectors for the canonicaliser alone are in tests/fixtures/canonical-json.json.
signing.base64: RFC 4648 section 4: standard alphabet, padded, one spelling per value

refused_public_keys.rule: Read the 32 key bytes as a little-endian integer and clear bit 255 (the sign of x); call the result y. Reject the key if y >= 2^255 - 19 (not a canonical encoding; code bad_key_encoding) or if y is one of the five values in small_order_y_hex (a point of small order; code weak_key). Do this yourself, before calling an Ed25519 library: libraries disagree.
refused_public_keys.small_order_y_note: 32-byte little-endian encodings with bit 255 clear, in the order of point orders 4, 1, 8, 8, 2. Each y belongs to a point and its negative, which covers all eight small-order points.

test_keys: Every 'seed_hex' is a published TEST private key (the 32-byte RFC 8032 seed). They exist so signing can be reproduced exactly. Never use them for anything else.
how_to_check_a_valid_entry: 2. Canonicalise what is left; the UTF-8 bytes must equal base64-decoded 'canonical_b64'.
3. Prepend the bytes of signing.prefix_hex; the result must equal 'signing_input_b64'.
4. base64-decode event.sig.key (32 bytes) and event.sig.value (64 bytes); they equal 'public_key_b64' and 'signature_b64', and the key passes signing.refused_public_keys.
5. Ed25519-verify the signature over the bytes of step 3 with that key: it must pass.
6. If you also sign: derive the key pair from 'seed_hex' and sign the bytes of step 3; Ed25519 is deterministic, so you must get exactly 'signature_b64'.
how_to_check_an_invalid_entry: Verification of 'event' must fail. 'expect' is the outcome code PortLock's verify_event reports (signature_mismatch, bad_signature_encoding, bad_key_encoding, weak_key, malformed_event, not_signed); other implementations need only reject, but should reject for the stated reason in 'why'. Every invalid event is a single change to the third valid event, except where 'why' says otherwise.

valid.name: minimal
valid.note: Smallest valid event: empty subject and data, no chain, ts 0.

valid.name: audit record with chain
valid.note: The envelope of record 3 of the audit chain in 'audit_chain'. chain.hash is that record's hash, and the id is derived from the host label and the hash (see the specification).

valid.name: non-ASCII text, escapes, key order and extreme integers
valid.note: Strings are signed as raw UTF-8 with no Unicode normalisation: the combining sequence stays two code points and the lock emoji is four bytes. Only the quote, the backslash and controls below U+0020 are escaped; U+007F, U+2028 and U+2029 are not. Object keys sort by code unit ('1' < 'B' < '_' < 'a' < 'aa' < 'b').

invalid.name: data changed after signing
invalid.why: One integer in data was changed; the signature no longer covers these bytes.

invalid.name: host label changed after signing
invalid.why: source.host was replaced.

invalid.name: chain removed after signing
invalid.why: chain was replaced by null: the event no longer commits to the audit log.

invalid.name: string normalised to NFC
invalid.why: data.combining was changed from 'e' + U+0301 to the single code point U+00E9. A verifier that normalises Unicode would wrongly accept one of the two.

invalid.name: signature bit flipped
invalid.why: The first byte of the signature has its lowest bit flipped.

invalid.name: key replaced by another valid key
invalid.why: sig.key names a different, valid public key; the signature was not made by it.

invalid.name: non-canonical signature scalar (S + L)
invalid.why: The group order L was added to the scalar half of a valid signature. RFC 8032 section 5.1.7 requires S < L; a verifier that skips the check accepts a second signature for the same event.

invalid.name: signed without the domain separator
invalid.why: A correct Ed25519 signature by the embedded key over the canonical JSON alone, without 'portlock/1/security-event' and the zero byte in front.

invalid.name: signature base64 without padding
invalid.why: sig.value has its '==' padding removed.

invalid.name: signature in the URL-safe alphabet
invalid.why: sig.value uses '-' and '_' instead of '+' and '/'.

invalid.name: signature of 63 bytes
invalid.why: sig.value decodes to 63 bytes.

invalid.name: key base64 with stray trailing bits
invalid.why: sig.key decodes to the right 32 bytes, but its last character has a non-zero unused bit, so it is a second spelling of the same key.

invalid.name: key of 31 bytes
invalid.why: sig.key decodes to 31 bytes.

invalid.name: key with surrounding whitespace
invalid.why: sig.key has a trailing newline.

invalid.name: unknown top-level member
invalid.why: An extra member was added beside the nine defined ones.

invalid.name: unsupported version
invalid.why: v is 2.

invalid.name: timestamp as a string
invalid.why: ts is an ISO 8601 string instead of integer milliseconds.

invalid.name: fractional number in data
invalid.why: data.size is 1.5; canonical JSON here has integers only.

invalid.name: integer outside the safe range
invalid.why: data.size is 2^53, one more than the largest integer every JSON implementation represents exactly.

invalid.name: wrong algorithm name
invalid.why: sig.alg is 'Ed25519' with a capital letter.

invalid.name: uppercase id
invalid.why: id uses uppercase hexadecimal digits.

invalid.name: wrong product
invalid.why: source.product is not 'portlock'.

invalid.name: signature removed
invalid.why: The sig member is absent.

invalid.name: public key is the identity point
invalid.why: sig.key is 01 00 ... 00, the neutral element of the curve, and sig.value is that same point followed by S = 0. No private key was involved: under this key the Ed25519 equation [S]B = R + [k]A holds for EVERY message, and a verifier that only evaluates the equation accepts any event 'signed' like this. Some widely used libraries do. Public keys of small order must be refused before the signature is looked at (specification section 4, step 4).

invalid.name: public key of order 8
invalid.why: sig.key is a point of order 8. sig.value (a small-order point as R, with S = 0) was found by trying the eight small-order points; no private key exists or was needed, and the plain Ed25519 equation holds for this event.

invalid.name: public key with a non-canonical y-coordinate
invalid.why: sig.key encodes y = p + 1 (p = 2^255 - 19), a second spelling of y = 1. A library that reduces y modulo p reads the identity point and then accepts this signature for every message; one that does not rejects the key. The y-coordinate must be below p (specification section 4, step 4).

audit_chain.description: A three-record audit log, so the chain a signed event points into can be checked too. hash = SHA-256(bytes.fromhex(prev_hash) || hashed_body), where hashed_body is the canonical JSON of the record's seq, ts, event_type, severity, actor, device_fp and data. The first prev_hash is genesis_hash = SHA-256('portlock-audit-v1'). The MAC key ratchets forward with every record: k_i = SHA-256(UTF8(ratchet_domain) || k_(i-1)), starting from initial_key_hex (k_0, anchored at record 0, never used as a MAC key itself), and mac = HMAC-SHA256(k_i, bytes.fromhex(hash)) for record i. mac_key_hex is k_i, given so each step can be checked.
audit_chain.initial_key_note: A published TEST key. Never use it for anything else.
